`plant` is an R package with compiled C++ code. This page gives you the shortest
route from a new R session to a working installation.

## Before you install

You need R 4.5.0 or newer and a compiler that supports C++20. Recent versions
of clang and gcc work on macOS and Linux. On Windows, install the version of
[Rtools](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/) that matches your R
installation.

`plant` is installed from GitHub rather than CRAN. Install the `remotes`
package once, then use it to install `plant` and its dependencies:

```r
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("traitecoevo/plant", dependencies = TRUE)
```

This installs the current default branch. If you need a particular release for
a reproducible analysis, choose a tag from the
[`plant` releases](https://github.com/traitecoevo/plant/releases) and include it
after `@`. For example:

```r
remotes::install_github("traitecoevo/plant@v2.0.0", dependencies = TRUE)
```

## Check the installation

Start a fresh R session and run:

```r
library(plant)
packageVersion("plant")

p <- scm_base_parameters("FF16")
p <- add_strategies(p, trait_matrix(0.0825, "lma"))
results <- run_scm(p, collect = TRUE)
```

If this completes without an error, the package and its compiled code are
working. `results` contains the changing state of a patch of plants; later
guides explain how to inspect it.

::: {.callout-tip}

## Installing from a local checkout

Building from a cloned repository is mainly useful when you want to contribute
to `plant` or test unreleased changes. Clone the repository, open R in that
directory, and run:

```r
devtools::install_deps()
devtools::install()
```

Use the GitHub installation above if you only want to run the model.
